title: BG2: The SpaceX IPO, Fable 5 & the AI Capex Reality Check

excerpts.label: Colossus 55% IRR — 'that math maths'
excerpts.insight: Baker: xAI's Google/Anthropic deals = highest operating profit per GW of anyone; 55% IRR on Colossus 1 vs 6-8% cost of debt. Terrestrial DC build speed is variable #1 for the IPO.
excerpts.pm_takeaway: The deal economics, not launch, are the IPO's near-term engine. Watch GW-online cadence.

excerpts.label: EWS: #4 hyperscaler in 30 days
excerpts.insight: Baker: SpaceX went from not-an-AI-hyperscaler to number four in 30 days, passing Oracle. Data centers are NOT commodities — Elon re-engineered DC design from first principles (122-day builds).
excerpts.pm_takeaway: EWS competes with every NeoCloud. Be selective in CRWV/Nebius/Iren tier — shortage rent gets arbitraged.

excerpts.label: Orbital math: $5B/GW space vs $25B ground
excerpts.insight: Fox: 100t Starship = ~5MW compute per launch → ~$5B/GW orbital capex vs $20-25B/GW terrestrial BOM. Ground inflationary, space deflationary. NOT needed for IPO valuation — pure call option.
excerpts.pm_takeaway: Orbital = 2028+ option gated on 2-stage rapid reuse. H2'26 second-stage recovery attempt is the binary.

excerpts.label: We don't know how smart models are
excerpts.insight: Baker via Noam Brown: nobody runs a model for a year before the next ships — snapshot benchmarks dead. Einstein-thinking-for-a-year thought experiment → 'however bullish I was on compute, I'm a lot more bullish.'
excerpts.pm_takeaway: Agent runtime × compute = new demand curve. Structurally bullish inference capacity.

excerpts.label: Frontier 90% of revenue, OSS 80% of tokens
excerpts.insight: Baker: both persist — and open source winning share is BULLISH for compute/hardware because less model-layer margin = more silicon spend. Harvey example: OSS + own data + router beat Opus at lower cost.
excerpts.pm_takeaway: Watch token-mix data (silicon data index OSS shift), not benchmarks — leading indicator for token pricing.

excerpts.label: 'That's a cute ASIC' — Jensen's OSS weapon
excerpts.insight: Baker: if customers compete with Nvidia via ASICs, Jensen can ship frontier open-source models and gut the margin pool funding those ASIC programs — and NVDA becomes a top cloud 'much faster than people think.'
excerpts.pm_takeaway: NVDA = laggard price (+10% YTD vs SMH +69%) + best narrative. The episode's implicit rotation target.

excerpts.label: 'The next-bottleneck game is over'
excerpts.insight: Baker: stocks went 'straight up a cliff — they're tired, they need to rest.' NVDA/AVGO ironically the laggards. Both funds trimmed (Altimeter large → medium-small) into seasonal weakness, CPI 4.2, oil $100.
excerpts.pm_takeaway: MU/MRVL/AMD = trail stops, don't initiate. Consolidation expected by the bulls themselves.

excerpts.label: Next $1T of revenue: 3 companies, half the time
excerpts.insight: Gerstner: Mag 7's last $1T of revenue took 7 years and created $17T of market cap. The forecast: SpaceX + Anthropic + OpenAI add the next $1T in 4-5 years. AI ends at 5-15% of global GDP.
excerpts.pm_takeaway: The size-of-prize frame — from a host with stakes in all three. Discount the messenger, keep the math.
